b1.text: Lantern is an accessibility platform, built for the whole enterprise.

b2.text: Documents. Slides. Course materials, even handwritten ones. Audio, and video that needs a transcript.

b3.text: Lantern brings it all together, in one place, and makes it functionally accessible, end to end.

b4.text: So, let's start with the campus lifecycle.

d2.text: Lantern starts at the front door of your domain, and follows every path, until it's found every site.

s2.text: It opens each site, follows every link, and gathers the files it finds.

s3.text: Every one is checked for accessibility problems, so you know exactly what needs attention.

c1.text: Do that for every site on campus, and something new appears:

c2.text: a complete inventory, of every file that must be made functionally accessible, across campus.

p2.text: For every site, Lantern builds a report: how many files it hosts, which aren't functionally accessible, which links are broken, and how it has changed over time.

p3.text: Every report lists each file, with a link to download it, and exactly what was found: tables with no header, images with no alt text, tagging that's missing.

p4.text: Reports are made to be shared, so each site owner knows exactly what to fix.

p5.text: A master report brings the whole campus together: which sites are the most accessible, how many documents each one hosts, and how many broken links they have.

p6.text: Next, we make those files functionally accessible.

r2.text: Lantern runs a vision model on university computers, to read each page the way a person would.

r3.text: It finds everything a document needs to be accessible: the headings, the lists, the tables, the reading order.

r4.text: And for every image, it writes a clear description, in plain, human words.

r5.text: Then it tags it all, so a screen reader can follow along.

r5b.text: All of it is built to the standards that apply: WCAG 2.1 level AA, and PDF/UA-1.

r6.text: It looks just the same. But now, anyone can use it, just as a sighted reader could.

t1.text: We tested that vision model on the hardest pages.

t2.text: Scanned documents. Handwritten ones. Pages with several tables. And scans taken at an angle.

t3.text: Each one is read the way it appears on the page.

v1.text: But how do we know it read the page correctly?

v2.text: Making a file functionally accessible runs in phases, and each one checks the model's reading against what is visible on the page.

v3.text: The words the model read are compared, one to one, with what a screen reader will say.

v4.text: The finished page is compared with the original, pixel for pixel, so nothing you can see has changed.

v5.text: And anything that can't be proved goes to a person, with the reasons attached.

f2.text: The vision model runs locally, so every file is read and processed on university computers.

f3.text: Nothing is sent to an outside service, and nothing is stored there.

f4.text: And no university file is ever used to train a model.

x1.text: And once it's functionally accessible, you simply replace the original.

x2.text: The new version looks exactly the same, but carries a complete accessibility layer on top, so it's readable by everyone.

cy2.text: Lantern runs again, on a schedule, so every new file is found, checked, and made functionally accessible, if it needs it.

w1.text: But your campus is more than documents on websites. That's where the Workbench comes in.

w2.text: Slide decks, made functionally accessible: alt text, proper titles, and a clear reading order.

w3.text: Presentations get captions, built from the audio in the slides.

w4.text: Audio and video get full transcripts.

w4b.text: For all of them, Lantern uses a speech-to-text model, to write the words from the file's own audio, along with their timestamps.

w5.text: And scanned, or handwritten, course materials, become clean documents, that you can edit, in Word or HTML.

w6.text: And the Workbench keeps growing, with more tools, and more features, on the way.

e1.text: Every document has something to say.

e2.text: Lantern makes sure, it reaches everyone.
